title: Group Policy: which settings reach Windows users and computers in Active Directory, and who sets them
summary: The page passes: Microsoft's documentation supports the configuration paths, automation, licensing statements and main processing rules. Minor corrections should clarify conflicting documentation on precedence and editing permissions, qualify the SYSVOL timing, and reconcile the reporting checklist with the controls table.

claims.claim: Group Policy is a Windows feature for central management of operating systems, applications and user settings.
claims.quote: Group Policy is a feature of Windows that provides centralized management and configuration of operating systems, applications, and user settings.

claims.claim: Group Policy applies registry-based Administrative Templates settings.
claims.quote: This article discusses how to use the new .admx and .adml files to create and administer registry-based policy settings in Windows.

claims.claim: Administrators put settings in GPOs and link them to Active Directory sites, domains or OUs to apply them to users and computers.
claims.quote: You can link GPOs to various levels within the AD hierarchy, such as sites, domains, and organizational units (OUs), which define their scope of application.

claims.claim: Precedence and security filtering determine which settings apply.
claims.quote: The GPO link with the lowest link order in the Group Policy Object Links list has precedence by default. Security filtering enables you to refine which users and computers receive and apply the policy settings in a GPO.

claims.claim: Each GPO has a Group Policy container stored in the domain partition of Active Directory.
claims.quote: The Group Policy container is stored in the domain partition of Active Directory

claims.claim: Each GPO has a Group Policy template stored in SYSVOL on each domain controller.
claims.quote: the Group Policy template is located in the SYSVOL folder on each domain controller (DC).

claims.claim: GPO settings are divided into computer and user settings.
claims.quote: Policy settings are categorized into those that apply to a computer and those that apply to a user.

claims.claim: Client-side extensions apply settings, including registry updates.
claims.quote: A Client-side extension (CSE) applies the specific settings dictated by the GPOs, managing tasks like registry updates and security configurations.

claims.where: What it is: Links and precedence
claims.claim: A GPO cannot be linked directly to a user object.
claims.quote: You can't link a GPO directly to a user object.

claims.where: What it is: Links and precedence
claims.claim: The local GPO is processed first.
claims.quote: Group Policy Objects (GPO) are processed in the following order: 1. The local GPO is applied.

claims.where: What it is: Links and precedence
claims.claim: After local policy, GPOs linked to sites, domains and OUs are processed in that order.
claims.quote: 2. GPOs linked to sites are applied. 3. GPOs linked to domains are applied. 4. GPOs linked to organizational units (OUs) are applied.

claims.where: What it is: Links and precedence
claims.claim: Settings from GPOs linked to Active Directory containers override local policy settings.
claims.quote: Policy settings from GPOs linked to AD containers override local policy settings.

claims.where: What it is: Links and precedence
claims.claim: Within one container, the link with the lowest link order has precedence.
claims.quote: The GPO link with the lowest link order in the Group Policy Object Links list has precedence by default.
claims.fix: Keep the lowest-link-order rule, but append: 'The cited Group Policy scope page's GPLink example instead labels GPO1, third in its link-order list, as highest precedence; this differs from the processing and GPMC pages.' The conflicting example is at https://learn.microsoft.com/windows-server/identity/ad-ds/manage/group-policy/group-policy-scope#gplink-attribute.

claims.where: What it is: Links and precedence; Governance controls
claims.claim: An Enforced GPO link takes precedence over Block Inheritance on a lower domain or OU.
claims.quote: Enforced is a link property and takes precedence over block policy inheritance, a container property.

claims.where: What it is: Security filtering; controls[2].note
claims.claim: Authenticated Users has Read and Apply group policy permissions on every GPO in the domain by default.
claims.quote: By default, the Authenticated Users group has Read and Apply group policy permissions for all GPOs in the domain.

claims.claim: A linked GPO applies to all users and computers in its container by default, unless administrators narrow its scope.
claims.quote: By default, a setting is applied to all user and computer objects within the container to which it's linked, but you can use security filtering to narrow the scope of the policy's application to a subset of users or computers.

claims.claim: Administrative Templates include .admx files.
claims.quote: Administrative Templates files are divided into .admx files and language-specific .adml files for use by Group Policy administrators.

claims.claim: Administrative Templates include language-specific .adml files.
claims.quote: Administrators can configure policies by using the language-specific .adml files and the language-neutral .admx files.

claims.claim: Microsoft publishes Windows Administrative Templates.
claims.quote: Administrative Templates (.admx) for Windows 11 2025 Update (25H2)

claims.where: What it is: Administrative Templates; summary
claims.claim: Microsoft Office has a separate set of templates for each release.
claims.quote: Microsoft Office has a separate set of ADMX/L files for each release.

claims.where: What it is: Administrative Templates; summary
claims.claim: Microsoft publishes separate Administrative Templates for Microsoft Edge.
claims.quote: There are two administrative templates for Microsoft Edge

claims.claim: The domain Central Store resides in SYSVOL.
claims.quote: To take advantage of the benefits of .admx files, you must create a Central Store in the sysvol folder on a Windows domain controller.

claims.claim: Central Store files replicate to all domain controllers in the domain.
claims.quote: The files that are in the Central Store are replicated to all domain controllers in the domain.

claims.claim: Edge policy settings can be stored under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Edge.
claims.quote: These policy settings are located at this registry path: HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Edge.

claims.claim: Computer policy settings apply at computer startup.
claims.quote: Group Policy for computer settings is applied when the computer starts.

claims.claim: User policy settings apply at user sign-in.
claims.quote: Policy settings are applied to computers when they start up and to users when they sign in.

claims.claim: Clients and servers check for Group Policy changes every 90 minutes.
claims.quote: By default, clients and servers check for changes to GPOs every 90 minutes using a randomized offset of up to 30 minutes.

claims.claim: The default background refresh has a random offset of up to 30 minutes.
claims.quote: The system might add a random time of up to 30 minutes to the refresh interval.

claims.claim: Domain controllers check for computer policy changes every five minutes.
claims.quote: Domain controllers check for computer policy changes every five minutes.

claims.claim: Cloud Policy reaches Microsoft 365 Apps users.
claims.quote: When a user signs into Microsoft 365 Apps for enterprise on a device, the policy settings roam to that device.

claims.quote: After you import them, you can create a device configuration policy that uses these settings, and then assign the policy to your managed devices. This feature applies to: Windows

claims.claim: Copilot's use of Edge page content is configurable through an Administrative Templates policy.
claims.quote: GP unique name: EdgeEntraCopilotPageContext; GP path (Mandatory): Administrative Templates/Microsoft Edge; GP ADMX file name: MSEdge.admx

claims.claim: Edge tab organisation is configurable through an Administrative Templates policy.
claims.quote: GP name: Enable tab organization suggestions; GP path (Mandatory): Administrative Templates/Microsoft Edge; GP ADMX file name: MSEdge.admx

claims.claim: OneDrive folder exclusions are configurable through its Group Policy Administrative Templates.
claims.quote: (EnableODIgnoreFolderListFromGPO) Exclude specific kinds of folders from being uploaded

claims.where: Why it matters; Risks and limits: Out-of-date Central Store; What to check
claims.claim: When using a Central Store, administrators copy updated template files into it to make new settings available.
claims.quote: To make this change, manually copy the updated .admx or .adml files from the PolicyDefinitions file on the local computer to the share sysvol folder

claims.claim: Group Policy is inherited and cumulative by default.
claims.quote: By default, Group Policy is inherited and cumulative

claims.claim: By default, domain-linked settings reach users and computers in the domain's child containers.
claims.quote: it affects all computers and users in an Active Directory (AD) container and its children.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risks and limits: Precedence surprises
claims.claim: A GPO with higher precedence can replace a policy value set by another GPO, including an Edge Copilot privacy policy.
claims.quote: The sequence of GPO processing is crucial because each subsequent policy application can override settings applied by earlier policies.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risks and limits: Cloud Policy wins
claims.claim: Cloud Policy settings take precedence over the same settings implemented through Group Policy.
claims.quote: policy settings implemented by using Cloud Policy take precedence over policy settings implemented by using Group Policy on Windows Server

claims.claim: Microsoft's Group Policy documentation does not publish a separate Group Policy licence.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Group Policy separate license price meter Windows GPMC'; read the Group Policy overview and GPMC prerequisites. They describe a Windows feature and management tools, not a separate Group Policy licence.

claims.claim: Microsoft's Group Policy documentation does not publish a separate Group Policy price.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Group Policy separate license price meter Windows GPMC'; read the Group Policy overview and GPMC documentation. Neither publishes a separate Group Policy price; search results supplied none.

claims.claim: Microsoft's Group Policy documentation does not publish a Group Policy meter.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Group Policy separate license price meter Windows GPMC'; read the Group Policy overview and GPMC documentation. Neither specifies a Group Policy consumption meter; search results supplied none.

claims.claim: GPMC is included with Windows Server and the Remote Server Administration Tools.
claims.quote: The GPMC is included with Windows Server and the Remote Server Administration Tools.

claims.claim: Domain-based Group Policy depends on domain controllers that store GPO components in Active Directory and SYSVOL.
claims.quote: GPOs are stored in both AD and the SYSVOL folder on each DC, facilitating centralized administration and policy enforcement.

claims.claim: The Microsoft Graph API for Intune, including the ADMX upload operation, requires an active Intune licence for the tenant.
claims.quote: The Microsoft Graph API for Intune requires an active Intune license for the tenant.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Out-of-date Central Store
claims.claim: SYSVOL is not updated automatically with new .admx or .adml files.
claims.quote: the sysvol folder isn't automatically updated to include the new .admx or .adml files.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Out-of-date Central Store
claims.claim: Windows ADMX download packages are supported only in the Central Store scenario, not as replacements in C:\Windows\PolicyDefinitions.
claims.quote: Use the ADMX download packages in only the Central Store scenario. Replacing files in c:\Windows\PolicyDefinitions isn't supported.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Changes are not immediate
claims.claim: A GPO change must replicate to the appropriate domain controller before clients can receive it at refresh.
claims.quote: Changes to Group Policy settings might not be immediately available on users' desktops because changes to the GPO must first replicate to the appropriate domain controller.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Changes are not immediate
claims.claim: Active Directory replication typically takes less than a minute between domain controllers within the same site.
claims.quote: By default, replication typically takes less than a minute between domain controllers within the same site.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Changes are not immediate
claims.claim: SYSVOL replication occurs every 15 minutes, in the paragraph's within-site timing comparison.
claims.quote: Within sites, replication occurs every 15 minutes. If the domain controllers are in different sites, the replication process occurs at set intervals based on site topology and schedule
claims.fix: Replace 'while SYSVOL replication occurs every 15 minutes' with 'while SYSVOL replication within a site occurs every 15 minutes'. This makes the within-site qualification explicit rather than leaving it attached only to the preceding AD comparison.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Changes are not immediate
claims.claim: Office policy changes generally take effect after Office apps restart.
claims.quote: Policies from Cloud Policy are applied only when the Office app is restarted. The behavior is the same as with Group Policy.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Changes are not immediate
claims.claim: Some Office privacy-control policies apply without restarting Office apps.
claims.quote: Some policies related to privacy controls will apply without restarting any Office apps.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Narrowing security filtering; controls[2].note; What to check
claims.claim: Computer accounts need Read permission on GPOs that apply to signed-in users.
claims.quote: the computer account has to have Read permissions for GPOs that apply to the signed-in user.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Narrowing security filtering
claims.claim: Removing Authenticated Users from Security Filtering removes both Read and Apply group policy permissions.
claims.quote: This action removes both the Read and the Apply group policy permissions from the group and all its members.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Edge recommended policies

claims.quote: Recommended policies provide a default setting that the user can override.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Intune import limits; controls[4].note; Open questions

claims.quote: This feature is in public preview.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Intune import limits; controls[4].note; Open questions
claims.claim: Intune accepts up to 20 imported ADMX files.
claims.quote: You can upload up to 20 ADMX files.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Intune import limits; controls[4].note

claims.quote: Each file must be 1 MB or smaller.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Intune import limits; controls[4].note; Open questions
claims.claim: Intune ADMX import supports only en-us ADML files.
claims.quote: Only en-us ADML files are supported.

claims.claim: Only domain administrators and enterprise administrators can link GPOs to domains and OUs by default.
claims.quote: By default, only domain administrators and enterprise administrators have this privilege for domains and OUs.

claims.claim: Editing a GPO needs Edit settings, delete and modify security permissions on it.
claims.quote: To use the GPMC, you must complete the following prerequisites. Have Edit settings, delete, and modify security permissions on the GPO.
claims.fix: Remove 'Editing a GPO needs the Edit settings, delete and modify security permissions on it.' The cited GPMC page supports that prerequisite list, but https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/security/application-security/application-control/app-control-for-business/applocker/export-an-applocker-policy-from-a-gpo instead says 'you must have the Edit Setting permission to edit a GPO'; the existing sentence presents the broader list as the minimum.

claims.claim: Importing ADMX files into Intune uses the Policy and Profile Manager built-in role.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Intune admin center with an account that has the Policy and Profile Manager built-in role.

claims.quote: Enforced is a link property

claims.where: Governance controls: Enforced and Block Inheritance

claims.quote: In the GPMC, an enforced link is indicated by a padlock icon on the linked policy.

claims.where: Governance controls: Enforced and Block Inheritance

claims.quote: The Set-GPInheritance cmdlet blocks or unblocks inheritance for a specified domain or organizational unit (OU).

claims.claim: gpupdate.exe triggers Group Policy refresh on the local computer.
claims.quote: Running gpupdate.exe triggers a policy refresh for the computer on which the command is run.

claims.claim: Invoke-GPUpdate triggers Group Policy refresh from PowerShell.
claims.quote: Use the Invoke-GPUpdate PowerShell cmdlet. You can use this cmdlet to trigger a refresh of the local computer or to trigger a refresh of a remote computer.

claims.claim: In GPMC, administrators can right-click an OU and select Group Policy Update.

claims.where: Governance controls: Refreshing and checking; What to check
claims.claim: gpresult reports the resultant policy settings that actually applied.
claims.quote: The gpresult command displays the resulting set of policy settings that were enforced on the computer for the specified user when the user signed in.

claims.claim: Get-GPResultantSetOfPolicy reports RSoP information.

claims.claim: RSoP modelling requires GPMC rather than Get-GPResultantSetOfPolicy.
claims.quote: This cmdlet provides only the logging results for a specified computer and user. You must use the GPMC to generate RSoP modeling information.

claims.claim: Get-GPOReport reports GPO links, security filtering, WMI filtering, delegation and settings.
claims.quote: The information that is reported for each GPO includes: details, links, security filtering, Windows Management Instrumentation (WMI) filtering, delegation, and computer and user configurations.

claims.where: Governance controls: Refreshing and checking; What to check
claims.claim: edge://policy on a device lists the Edge policies applied there.
claims.quote: On a target client device, open Microsoft Edge and go to edge://policy to see all policies that are applied.

claims.claim: Get-GPOReport can report across all GPOs.
claims.quote: You can specify the All parameter to generate a report for every GPO in the domain

claims.claim: Microsoft does not publish one index identifying the first Administrative Templates release for every Copilot-related Edge, Office and OneDrive policy.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Copilot Edge Office OneDrive policy Administrative Templates release version index first introduced'; read Central Store, Edge policy references and returned Edge/OneDrive release-note excerpts. Found product-specific material, not the claimed cross-product index.

claims.claim: The pages researched do not establish which value wins when Intune and a GPO set the same Edge policy on a hybrid-joined device.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Microsoft Edge policy precedence Intune MDM GPO hybrid joined same policy'; read Edge configuration and returned Intune/Edge management excerpts. They describe equivalent management and cloud/platform precedence, not the Intune-versus-GPO winner for this case.

claims.claim: GPMC provides Site, domain or OU > Link an Existing GPO.
claims.quote: Right-click a site, domain, or OU item, and then select Link an Existing GPO.

claims.claim: New-GPO -Name <GPO name> | New-GPLink -Target <distinguished name of site, domain or OU> -LinkEnabled Yes creates and enables a GPO link.
claims.quote: New-GPO -Name "MyGPO" | New-GPLink -Target "ou=MyOU,dc=contoso,dc=com" -LinkEnabled Yes; Specifies the LDAP distinguished name of the site, domain, or OU to which to link the GPO.

claims.claim: The Group Policy Management Editor path Computer Configuration > Policies > Administrative Templates > Microsoft Edge > policy reaches an Edge policy.
claims.quote: open the Group Policy Management Editor from Windows Administrative Tools and expand Computer Configuration > Policies > Administrative Templates > Microsoft Edge.

claims.claim: Set-GPRegistryValue -Name <GPO name> -Key <registry key> -ValueName <value name> -Value <value> -Type <type> configures a registry-based GPO policy setting.
claims.quote: Set-GPRegistryValue [-Name] <String> -Key <String> [-ValueName <String[]>] [-Value <PSObject>] [-Type <RegistryValueKind>]; One or more registry values by passing the Key, ValueName, Value, and Type parameters.

claims.claim: GPMC provides Group Policy Objects > GPO > Scope > Security Filtering for a GPO's security filter.
claims.quote: In GPMC, on the Scope tab for the GPO, you add contoso_user_group to the Security Filtering list.

claims.quote: Set-GPPermission [-Name] <String> -PermissionLevel <GPPermissionType> -TargetName <String> -TargetType <PermissionTrusteeType>; The acceptable values for this parameter are: GpoRead, GpoApply, GpoEdit, GpoEditDeleteModifySecurity, None.

claims.quote: Friendly Name | Set Group Policy refresh interval for computers; Location | Computer Configuration; Path | System > Group Policy

claims.claim: ./Device/Vendor/MSFT/Policy/Config/ADMX_GroupPolicy/GroupPolicyRefreshRate configures the computer background refresh interval through MDM.
claims.quote: ./Device/Vendor/MSFT/Policy/Config/ADMX_GroupPolicy/GroupPolicyRefreshRate; This policy setting specifies how often Group Policy for computers is updated while the computer is in use (in the background).

claims.claim: The computer refresh interval setting accepts 0 to 64,800 minutes.
claims.quote: If you enable this setting, you can specify an update rate from 0 to 64,800 minutes (45 days).

claims.claim: Microsoft Intune admin center provides Devices > Manage devices > Configuration > Import ADMX > Import.
claims.quote: Select Devices > Manage devices > Configuration > Import ADMX tab > Import

claims.claim: POST /beta/deviceManagement/groupPolicyUploadedDefinitionFiles uploads an ADMX definition file through Microsoft Graph.
claims.quote: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/deviceManagement/groupPolicyUploadedDefinitionFiles

claims.claim: The ADMX upload request body's content property holds the ADMX file contents.
claims.quote: content | Binary | The contents of the uploaded ADMX file.

claims.quote: groupPolicyUploadedLanguageFiles | groupPolicyUploadedLanguageFile collection | The list of ADML files associated with the uploaded ADMX file.

claims.quote: What to check: 'Run Get-GPOReport across all GPOs.' The table contains linking, registry settings, security filtering, background refresh and Intune ADMX import, but no GPO reporting row.
claims.fix: Remove the 'Run Get-GPOReport across all GPOs. For each Edge, Office or OneDrive policy, find every GPO that sets it, and note its links and link order.' checklist bullet. Keep the verified reporting explanation in Governance controls; do not add a table row.
